title: Pendulum
rule: Each panel is one swing of the clock's pendulum, which crosses every gutter; the count of swings is the page's only measure of time.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p93_pendulum.py (b1m2 cut-paper figure model printed in ink, as pages 06/46; ring disc: films/swarm/anemic-cinema/optics.render_rings)

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

made: eight panels in four tiers of two on the LoC 1934 sheet; each panel an upright ink print of the b1m2 HANDMADE cut-paper office model (agent in waistcoat and shirt sleeves with pencil, stranger in cloche hat behind the TICKET OFFICE window, desk, memo pencilled 4:15 in red, wall clock at 4:10 drawn WITHOUT a pendulum, cupboard opening on its left jamb, SERVICE door with a red-lettered SERVICE card), the ANRC 1922 key cutout in brass with a SERVICE tag

the pendulum: a HANDMADE cut-card brass rod pinned with a brass pin in the gutter above each tier (tier 1 hangs from the clock case cut in the header), crossing the gutter into the panel; its bob a brass card disc printed with the anemic-cinema O_A engraved eccentric-ring disc (procedural), turned a step per swing, with the swing number 1-8 in red at its hub
the bob is on the left in left panels and on the right in right panels; in every panel a pencil-dotted arc and a ghost ring show the swing coming across the centre gutter from the other side

captions on pasted slips begin 'Swing 1.' ... 'Swing 8.'; no clock time or interval is stated in any caption (the clock face in panel 4 and the memo's 4:15 are objects of the story, and the canon answer names 4:10)
the four canon lines verbatim in cut-paper balloons (panels 3, 4, 5, 8); header in the pen hand: 'The station clock's pendulum: / one panel, one swing.'; folio '93 / Pendulum'

events.E0: swings 1-2: memo on the desk (4:15 in red); he gets up and sets off
events.E1: swing 3: question at the TICKET OFFICE window
events.E2: swing 4: he looks up at the clock (4:10); answer
events.E3: swing 5: thanks; swing 6: she turns away
events.E4: swing 6: on to the cupboard; swing 7: he opens it, the brass key on its hook tagged SERVICE
events.E5: swing 8: pencil to chin, forgetting line; caption: the key stays, the door stays shut

beat: the pendulum swings once per frame: each frame adds the next panel and the bob arrives on the other side, its dotted path crossing the centre gutter
beat_frames: b01: swing 1, panel 1 filled, bob left
b02: swing 2, panel 2 filled, bob right
b03: swing 3, panel 3 filled, bob left
b04: swing 4, panel 4 filled, bob right
b05: swing 5, panel 5 filled, bob left
b06: swing 6, panel 6 filled, bob right
b07: swing 7, panel 7 filled, bob left
b08: swing 8, panel 8 filled, bob right

self_check.check: A reader sees the pendulum alternate sides from panel to panel.
self_check.evidence: perceptually judged by the maker at full size: bob left, right, left, right... with numbered bobs 1-8; captions measure time only in swings
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker

weaknesses: four pivots (one per tier) rather than one continuous pendulum: each tier shows the same pendulum again; the rod crosses the horizontal gutter and the swing path the vertical gutter, not literally every gutter
alternation coincides with the two-column layout, so 'left/right' is also simply the column; the numbered bob and dotted path carry the swing
silhouette figures are small (about 300 px); the stranger in panel 6 is half hidden behind the rod; key and SERVICE tags need a close look
panel 8's caption is cut down to 'The key stays; the door stays shut.' to clear his head
spiral-disc medium is present only as the ring-printed bobs; the disc does not visibly spiral in a still
